couple.names: John Michael Lien and Diana Duchicela Guajan

ceremony.address: Carchi y Venezuela, Centro Histórico, Quito, Ecuador

reception.address: García Moreno N5-16 y Chile, Plaza de la Independencia, Centro Histórico, Quito, Ecuador

wedding.walkBetweenVenues: About 8 minutes on foot — the two venues are both in the historic Old Town.

travel.altitude: Quito sits at about 9,350 ft / 2,850 m. Mild altitude effects (shortness of breath, fatigue) are common in the first 48 hours. Arrive early if possible, hydrate, eat light, take it easy.
travel.weatherMarch: Wet season. Temperatures 50-69 F / 10-21 C. Pack layers, rain jacket, comfortable walking shoes, and sunscreen — UV is intense at altitude.
travel.currency: U.S. Dollar. Small bills are useful for taxis, markets, and tips.
travel.visa: U.S. citizens generally do not need a visa for tourist stays up to 90 days. Other passports — check the Ecuadorian embassy guidance for your country.
travel.languageNote: Many tourism providers and hotels in Quito work with English-speaking guests. Learning hola, gracias, por favor is appreciated.

lodging.recommendation: We recommend staying in or near Old Town for the easiest wedding-day logistics. See the Travel page for suggested 4-star and 5-star options.
lodging.shuttle: Hotel Plaza Grande can help arrange airport shuttle service; contact the hotel directly when booking. Other hotels may offer similar services.

dayOf.dressCode: Formal or cocktail attire. For the church ceremony, please choose respectful coverage (shoulders and knees covered).
dayOf.kidsPolicy: Children are warmly welcome at both the ceremony and the reception. Guests should note kids on their RSVP so planning is accurate.
dayOf.plusOnes: Plus-ones are welcome — every invited guest is encouraged to bring whoever they would like to celebrate with. Please add the plus-one's name on the RSVP.
dayOf.meals: Multiple options will be available. Please indicate dietary needs on your RSVP.
dayOf.photography: Personal photos welcome during cocktails and reception. Please respect the officiant's request to refrain from flash photography during the ceremony itself.

timeZone.name: Ecuador Time
timeZone.note: Ecuador does not observe daylight saving time. All published wedding times are Ecuador time (ECT, UTC-5) year-round.

sightseeing.intro: Quito and the surrounding area offer many memorable sightseeing options for guests extending their trip.

options.name: Old Town walking tour
options.details: Plaza Grande, Iglesia de La Compañía (dazzling gold-leaf interior, small entry fee), San Francisco church (free), and Calle La Ronda for cafes and shops.

options.name: TelefériQo cable car
options.details: Cable car to about 3,945 m above the city for sweeping views; round-trip about $8.50. Go early before clouds build.

options.name: Mitad del Mundo
options.details: Equator monument about 45 minutes north of Quito; entry around $5. Nearby Museo Solar Inti Ñan offers playful gravity demonstrations.

options.name: Mindo Cloud Forest
options.details: Birding and waterfalls about 2 hours northwest. 450+ species recorded. Best with a local guide in the morning.

options.name: Otavalo Market (Saturday)
options.details: Famous Andean textile market about 2 hours north of Quito. Best on Saturdays.

options.name: Galápagos extension
options.details: Multi-day add-on requiring a domestic flight from UIO. Plan additional yellow-fever-vaccine guidance if extending.

options.name: Cuenca or Amazon extensions
options.details: Cuenca is a colonial UNESCO city; Amazon lodges via Coca. Both need flights and extra days.

health.vaccinesNote: No special vaccines are required for Quito itself. Yellow fever vaccine is recommended if extending to the Amazon (and required by some countries on re-entry).
health.waterNote: Most travelers drink bottled or filtered water in Ecuador. Hotels typically provide bottled water in rooms.
health.sunNote: UV is intense at altitude — use SPF 30+ even on cloudy days, and bring sunglasses and a hat.
health.altitudeReminder: Quito sits at about 2,850 m / 9,350 ft. Arrive a day or two early if possible, hydrate, eat lightly, and avoid alcohol the first night.
health.pharmaciesNote: Pharmacies ("farmacias") are common in Quito. Many staff speak basic English and can help with common over-the-counter needs.

connectivity.intro: Staying connected in Ecuador is easy with several options.

options.name: US carrier roaming
options.details: Most US plans (T-Mobile, Verizon, AT&T) include Ecuador data, though speeds may be slower than at home. Check your specific plan before traveling.

options.name: eSIM (recommended)
options.details: Airalo and Holafly offer Ecuador eSIMs from about $5-15 for 1-2 GB. Install before flying and activate on arrival.

options.name: Local SIM
options.details: Claro and Movistar sell prepaid SIMs at UIO airport for around $10 with a few GB of data. Bring an unlocked phone.

options.name: WiFi
options.details: Most hotels, cafés, and restaurants in Quito have free WiFi available to customers.

registry.note: Your presence is the greatest gift; any contribution is deeply appreciated.

heritage.summary: Diana's roots are in Otavalo, an Andean Kichwa community known for music and weaving. The celebration honors kuyay (Kichwa for love) — love of family, place, and the people who join us in Quito.

contact.cancellationOrConcerns: Please reach out to John or Diana directly as early as possible so we can update counts.
